learningObjective: Compute a GPU's Roofline ridge point from published peak throughput and memory bandwidth, and reason about how the ridge shifts across precisions.

canonicalClaims.claim: Ridge point equals peak compute divided by peak memory bandwidth, and increases as the precision path moves to lower-bit operands (FP16 → FP8 → FP4) because peak compute rises while HBM bandwidth stays fixed.
conditions: Compute peak is measured with the same math path (Tensor Core) whose ridge is being computed.
Memory bandwidth reference is HBM (or whichever tier the AI is measured against).
nonImplications: Does not imply that a kernel automatically saturates the higher-precision peak at higher ridge; achievable throughput still requires high AI.
Does not imply that ridges are meaningful without matching AI accounting to the same memory tier.

misconceptions.claim: Ridge point is a hardware-fixed value independent of numerical precision.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ridge point uses the peak compute of a specific precision path; different precisions produce different peaks and hence different ridges on the same GPU.

misconceptions.claim: Halving operand bytes halves the ridge point.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Operand byte width affects AI (algorithmic side); ridge is compute/BW on the hardware side. In fact halving operand width usually doubles the hardware peak throughput, raising ridge.

misconceptions.claim: Ridge point can be computed from L2 or SMEM bandwidth without changing meaning.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Using L2/SMEM bandwidth defines a different Roofline; AI must be measured against the same memory tier, otherwise ridge comparisons are inconsistent.

misconceptions.claim: Sparse Tensor Core peaks should be used to compute the everyday FP16 ridge point.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Sparse peaks assume structured 2:4 sparsity and only apply to kernels using that path; using them for a dense kernel gives an unreachable ridge.

implementationFacts: H100 SXM5 (dense): FP16 ridge ≈ 295 FLOP/byte; FP8 ridge ≈ 590 FLOP/byte.
performanceScenarios: Moving from FP16 to FP8 GEMMs raises the ridge, so an FP16-compute-bound kernel may become memory-bound at FP8 if AI does not scale with precision.
